songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Scorching Dark Star→Stephan→Eleven chain, fierce Alligator jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a classic early‑'69 run with a monster Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven → Turn On Your Lovelight sequence and an explosive Alligator → Caution → Feedback climax. Jerry’s guitar shines when it cuts through the mix, while Bill and Mickey drive the jams with relentless power. Recording quality is uneven – the organ sits too forward – but the performances more than make up for it.
ai_show_review.review:
On January 25, 1969 at San Francisco’s Avalon Ballroom the Dead hit a creative peak that still feels fresh. The first set rolls out a searing Dark Star that morphs into Saint Stephen and then rockets through The Eleven before resolving in an uplifting Turn On Your Lovelight – a sequence many fans cite as one of the era’s finest moments. Despite Tom Constanten’s organ dominating the mix, his swirling runs add an unmistakable texture to the improvisations, and Phil’s bass on Lovelight provides a melodic anchor. 

The second set is where the band truly lets loose. After Dupree's Diamond Blues and Doin' That Rag, they launch into a double‑Alligator saga that builds through a thunderous drum duet into Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) and erupts into a feedback‑laden climax before closing with a gentle “And We Bid You Good Night.” Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart play their A$$ off, especially on the Alligator‑Caution stretch. While the soundboard recordings suffer from an over‑loud organ and occasional mix quirks that bury Jerry’s guitar at times, the musical intensity and historic improvisational peaks make this a must‑listen show.

best_recording.reason: Despite mix quirks, it’s the most complete soundboard source and is flagged as the community’s preferred version.

key_highlights: Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven → Turn On Your Lovelight sequence
Alligator → Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Feedback climax
Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart deliver powerhouse drumming throughout
Tom Constanten’s organ runs add texture, though they dominate the mix

band_performance.Jerry: Guitar often buried by the forward organ mix but bursts through with fantastic tone on The Eleven and during the Alligator jams, delivering his signature lyrical solos when audible.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a solid, melodic bass foundation; his work on Lovelight is particularly praised for its drive and fluidity.
band_performance.Bob: Vocals become clearer later in the set, especially on Turn On Your Lovelight, holding up despite overall mix challenges.
band_performance.Tom: Organ is excessively forward – likely a Vox Continental with occasional synth‑like overlay – which can overwhelm but also supplies distinctive swirling textures throughout the show.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are powerful and relentless, propelling the Alligator and Caution sections with thunderous energy.
band_performance.Billy: Pairs with Mickey to play "their A$$ off," especially evident during the high‑octane jam sequences.

must_listen_sequences: And We Bid You Good Night
